summary: Examples for managing apt keys: a keyless approach using get_url plus a signed-by repository, adding keys by id from a keyserver or URL, removing a key, adding from file contents, using a specific keyring, and adding a key file on the remote.
questions: How do I add a third-party apt repo without apt_key?
How do I use signed-by with a key downloaded to /etc/apt/keyrings?
How do I remove an apt signing key by fingerprint?
How do I add a key from a file on the control node?
Should armored keys use .asc or .gpg extension?

answer_card.title: apt_key examples and the signed-by alternative
answer_card.answer_md:
Preferred approach without apt_key:
```yaml
- ansible.builtin.get_url:
    url: https://keyserver.ubuntu.com/pks/lookup?op=get&search=0x36a1...
    dest: /etc/apt/keyrings/myrepo.asc
- ansible.builtin.apt_repository:
    repo: "deb [arch=amd64 signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/myrepo.asc] https://download.example.com/linux/ubuntu {{ ansible_distribution_release }} stable"
```
Armored keys use `.asc`, binary `.gpg`.

apt_key forms:
```yaml
- apt_key: {keyserver: keyserver.ubuntu.com, id: 36A1D786...}
- apt_key: {url: https://ftp-master.debian.org/keys/archive-key-6.0.asc}
- apt_key: {id: 0x9FED2BCB..., state: absent}
- apt_key: {data: "{{ lookup('ansible.builtin.file', 'apt.asc') }}"}
```
